name: TN-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+29 district partisanship in deep-red East Tennessee
Incumbent Harshbarger with large cash advantage
Prediction markets price Republican win at 98%
model.rationale: The R+29 lean, Harshbarger's incumbency and roughly 12-to-1 fundraising edge, and markets pricing her at 98% all point to a safe Republican hold with no polling or ratings suggesting otherwise.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or a late outside-spending surge for Burke would be the only plausible path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Diana Harshbarger seeks a third term in a northeastern Tennessee district that is among the most Republican in the country, with a partisan lean of about 29 points to the right. She enters the general election with roughly $2 million on hand after raising over $1.2 million, while Democratic nominee Kristi Burke has raised about $102,000 and had just $14,000 in the bank. Several independent candidates are on the ballot but show no fundraising or organized support.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give the Republican about a 98% chance of winning. The forecast expects Harshbarger to win by roughly 22 points, with the challenger's main opportunity being a strong national Democratic wave, which this district's fundamentals make unlikely to matter much.
